entries.topic: Load GLB as Scene when hierarchy/instances matter
entries.content: Use load_scene for GLB/glTF when multiple geometries, transforms or instances must be preserved. Loading as a single mesh can irreversibly concatenate information needed for asset separation.

Determine whether the loaded object is a Scene or Trimesh before applying mesh-only operations. Scene geometry is referenced through a transform graph and may contain repeated instances of the same geometry.

entries.topic: Preserve raw mesh data when requested
entries.content: Trimesh performs light processing by default, including cleanup such as merging coincident vertices. Use process=False when an extraction pipeline must preserve source indexing/topology until it explicitly decides what cleanup is safe.

A Scene can store geometry separately from node transforms. When splitting/exporting objects, apply or preserve each graph transform intentionally instead of treating geometry coordinates as already world-space.
Do not infer game-scale corrections from visual appearance. If source units are known, use explicit unit metadata/conversion and validate expected bounding dimensions after conversion.

Export GLB from a validated Scene after transforms, hierarchy and geometry assignments are correct. Treat successful serialization as a format check, then separately validate the resulting asset in Blender/Godot.

Use connectivity-based split operations only when disconnected components correspond to the desired asset separation. Do not assume every disconnected island is a semantic object such as a wheel or chassis.
